sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Wet-season and dry-season remote-imagery comparison with two limited ground-control visits

**Instrumentation:** Multispectral image set, soil-conductivity sled, shallow magnetometer array, and manual surface profile

**Study boundary:** A coded floodplain sector containing repeated linear relief and discontinuous vegetation bands.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Geometric response:** Twenty-seven linear segments retained a common 3.6-metre spacing despite crossing present drainage and cultivation boundaries. Eleven terminated at near-right-angle returns.

**Surface restoration:** A documented 19-metre maintenance strip was mechanically leveled between visits. Eleven of twelve crossed segments reappeared within 23 days at the prior stationing, with a median recovered relief of 31 millimetres. No corresponding deposited volume was found at the strip margins.

**Subsurface response:** Shallow conductivity and magnetic gradients followed selected segments before and after leveling but did not identify masonry, continuous metal, or a modern pipe network.

**Seasonal behavior:** Vegetation contrast reversed between wet and dry observations while the geometric boundary remained stable.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Historic drainage, former planting beds, buried combustion features, and repeated soil compaction can account for the original pattern. Settlement and differential moisture were tested against the maintenance strip.

**Confirmed exception:** Neither process accounts for restoration of the leveled relief at its former stations without measurable lateral soil transfer. The observations establish pattern reconstitution; they do not establish an age, builder, or purpose.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** A fixed-spacing surface and shallow-field pattern reconstituted after documented mechanical removal. The process is repeatable at the monitored strip and has no assigned transport mechanism.

**Action:** Preserve non-invasive baselines. A second controlled leveling trial requires simultaneous mass survey, time-lapse imaging, and separate archaeological and land-access review.

**Hazard status:** No field hazard above ordinary floodplain conditions was established.
